drafts.lead: Jason, Ready to Roll Transportation — challenged how we source the '10 to 30 corporate travel managers' and what verification looks like
drafts.body:
Jason,

You are right that the claim is easy to make, so here is the unflattering detail.

They are not inbound. Nobody is raising a hand and asking to be introduced to you. We build a list of corporate travel managers, executive assistants and event coordinators at companies that fit your profile, filtered on things we can actually observe: headcount, offices in your service area, whether they run events, whether they have someone with travel or facilities in their title. Then we email them in your name from separate sending domains, so readytoroll.com is never put at risk.

Verification is the reply. Someone at a real company, with a real title, writing back to say they are interested. That is the only signal we count, and it is the one you can check yourself because it lands in your inbox rather than being reported to you in a dashboard.

The 10 to 30 figure is conversations started over a month, not meetings held and not signed contracts. I would rather tell you that now than have you find out in week six.

If that is a model you can work with:

• Monday, August 17 at 1:30 PM EDT
• Tuesday, August 18 at 1:30 PM EDT

And if it is not, say so plainly and I will leave you alone.

Georgia

drafts.lead: Barry Rowley, Pearl Logic — works with third parties strictly on a pay-for-performance channel partner model
drafts.body:
Barry,

Thank you for laying it out so clearly, and I will do the same.

Your Channel Partner Program is built for partners who sell on your behalf and get paid when a client signs. We are not that. We do not sell your product, we do not own the relationship, and we do not want a share of your revenue. We run the outbound so the conversations arrive with your team, and we charge a flat monthly fee for doing it whether or not those conversations close.

So on a pure pay-for-performance basis we are not a fit, and I would rather say that than dress it up.

One alternative if a recurring fee is the objection rather than the principle: we build the outbound system, run it until it produces, then hand it to you outright. You own it and everything it generates from that point, with nothing ongoing to us.

If that is worth a conversation, say so. If not, no hard feelings and I will close the file.

Christina
